Title: Identifiability and Stability of Generative Drifting with Companion-Elliptic Kernel Families
Text:
Identifiability and Stability of Generative Drifting with
Companion-Elliptic Kernel Families
Lee Hak Geun∗
Abstract
This paper analyzes identifiability and stability for the drifting field underlying distributional
matching in the Generative Drifting framework of Deng et al. [1].
First, we introduce the
class of companion-elliptic kernels, which includes the Laplace kernel and is characterized by a
second-order elliptic coupling between each kernel κ in this class and its companion function
η. For each kernel in this class and each pair of Borel probability measures, we prove that the
drifting field vanishes if and only if the two probability measures are equal. We further show
that this class consists precisely of Gaussian kernels and Matérn kernels with ν ≥1/2. Second,
by constructing counterexamples, we exhibit sequences for which mass escapes to infinity while
the field tends to zero; in particular, control of the field norm alone does not guarantee weak
convergence. Nevertheless, we prove that the only possible mode of failure is confined to the
one-dimensional ray {c p : 0 ≤c ≤1}. Consequently, weak convergence can be restored by
imposing an asymptotic lower bound on the intrinsic overlap scalar, a linear observable defined
by the kernel and the target measure.

Introduction
1.1
Theoretical point of departure
Deng et al. [1] adopt the viewpoint that generative modeling is the problem of learning the push-
forward of a prior distribution. More precisely, given a prior law pε and a generator fθ : RC →RD,
the model law is defined by
qθ = fθ#pε.
In this setting, diffusion models [21, 22] and flow matching [23] implement complex pushforwards
through multi-step inference-time updates. By contrast, drifting keeps inference single-step and
instead evolves the pushforward law itself during training. Accordingly, Deng et al. [1] describe the
training process as producing a sequence of parameters θ0, θ1, θ2, . . . together with a corresponding
chain of laws
qi = [fθi]#pε,
whose evolution is described directly at the level of distributions.

This paper addresses two questions.
(Q1) Field identifiability. Does the implication
Vp,q ≡0 =⇒p = q
hold? This is the problem posed by Deng et al. [1].
(Q2) Field stability. In which topology, and with what additional scalar observable, does

Our results are as follows. For the Laplace kernel, the implication in (Q1) holds for the full class
of Borel probability measures. Moreover, the same mechanism extends to the entire translation-
invariant companion-elliptic kernel family. For (Q2), the corresponding stability statement fails
without an additional observable: neither locally uniform (compact-open) control nor global L∞
control implies weak convergence. However, within the companion-elliptic class, the only possible
limiting defect lies on the one-dimensional ray {c p : 0 ≤c ≤1}. Adding a single scalar observable
that separates the target point from all other points on this ray restores weak convergence.

Related work
Our starting point is the work of Deng et al. [1], which introduced the drifting field and documented
its empirical behavior. Several recent works have clarified related aspects of drifting. Li and Zhu
reinterpreted drifting through a long–short flow-map factorization [14]. Lai et al. showed that, for
the Gaussian kernel, drifting coincides exactly with a score mismatch and that, in an appropriate
asymptotic regime, it provides a controlled approximation in the Laplace-kernel setting [13]. Turan
and Ovsjanikov derived a Gaussian-kernel score-matching identity and developed its spectral and
variational consequences [20]. These score-based reinterpretations connect directly to the classical
3


principle of score matching [26].
Cao, Wei, and Liu placed drifting in a broader Wasserstein
gradient-flow framework for KDE-approximated divergences [2, 9], while explicitly noting that
the Laplace kernel does not belong to their kernel class [9]. He et al. proved identifiability for a
Sinkhorn-normalized two-sided variant, thereby highlighting the gap between one-sided and two-
sided formulations [12]. Within the one-sided raw drifting formulation of Deng et al. [1], the present
paper establishes identifiability on the full space of Borel probability measures and characterizes
the stability obstruction caused by mass escape. Our results cover both the Laplace kernel and the
companion-elliptic kernel family that contains it.

Conclusion
This paper resolves the identifiability and stability problems for the drifting field underlying the
Generative Drifting framework.
In particular, within the one-sided raw drifting formulation of
Deng et al. [1], we settle the remaining converse problem on the full space of Borel probability
measures: for both the Laplace kernel and the companion-elliptic kernel family that contains it,
Vp,q ≡0 implies p = q. To prove this, we introduced a new framework, the companion-elliptic
kernel class, in which a kernel and its companion function are linked through a second-order
elliptic operator.
We further showed that this class consists precisely of Gaussian kernels and
Matérn kernels with ν ≥1/2.
Concerning the asymptotic stability of drifting fields, we identified an additional limitation: even
when the global field norm tends to zero, weak convergence of the underlying probability measures
need not follow, because mass may escape to infinity. Nevertheless, we proved that the limiting
defect caused by such mass escape is confined to the one-dimensional ray consisting of scalar
multiples c · p of the target distribution. Building on this observation, we introduced the intrinsic
overlap scalar, a scalar observable defined directly by the drifting kernel, and showed that imposing
an asymptotic lower bound on this scalar at its target value prevents mass from escaping and
restores weak convergence. Taken together, these results provide a rigorous theoretical foundation
for the convergence analysis of Generative Drifting models.

Abstract: This paper analyzes identifiability and stability for the drifting field underlying distributional matching in the Generative Drifting framework of Deng et al. [1]. First, we introduce the class of companion-elliptic kernels, which includes the Laplace kernel and is characterized by a second-order elliptic coupling between each kernel κ in this class and its companion function η. For each kernel in this class and each pair of Borel probability measures, we prove that the drifting field vanishes if and only if the two probability measures are equal. We further show that this class consists precisely of Gaussian kernels and Matérn kernels with ν ≥1/2. Second, by constructing counterexamples, we exhibit sequences for which mass escapes to infinity while the field tends to zero; in particular, control of the field norm alone does not guarantee weak convergence. Nevertheless, we prove that the only possible mode of failure is confined to the one-dimensional ray {c p : 0 ≤c ≤1}. Consequently, weak convergence can be restored by imposing an asymptotic lower bound on the intrinsic overlap scalar, a linear observable defined by the kernel and the target measure.
